I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My fields sit on the North China Plain — flat, deep loam, with good water-holding capacity but a water table that I've watched drop every decade. At my age I'm not experimenting much. I know what this land does.

The only sensible rotation here is **winter wheat followed by summer maize** on the same plots. Everyone around me does it, the market is stable, and my body still handles it. I've got 15 mu under my own name plus another few I help manage, so I'll work 15 mu myself.

For wheat, I'll use the improved semi-dwarf variety my seed cooperative has been pushing — Jimai 22 or similar. Rotary till after the maize harvest to chop the stalks under, then sow in mid-October. I apply base fertilizer before seeding, then topdress nitrogen at jointing. I'll irrigate twice: once before the ground freezes (冬水) and once at jointing. The aquifer situation worries me so I skip the optional grain-fill irrigation unless it's a real drought year. Two pesticide passes — a herbicide early and a fungicide hit when powdery mildew or rust shows up in May.

For maize, I go straight in after wheat harvest with no-till seeding — saves fuel and the residue helps moisture retention. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, which I've seen perform consistently. Summer rains usually cover most of my water needs so I only irrigate once at establishment if the soil is dry. One pesticide application for corn borer or armyworm if scouting warrants it.

I don't chase maximum yield. At 63, I manage for reliable income and reduced physical load. 450 kg/mu wheat and 550 kg/mu maize is realistic and I'm satisfied with that.
